title: Improving Physical Activity and Gait Symmetry After Total Knee Arthroplasty
brief_summary: The purpose of this pilot study is to examine the effectiveness of the Physical Activity and Symmetry (PAS) program, compared to an attention (ATT)control group, for patients with post-total knee arthroplasty (TKA). The investigators hypothesize that the PAS treatment will result in meaningful improvements in physical activity (PA) and joint loading symmetry compared to the ATT group.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients receiving post-total knee arthroplasty (TKA) physical therapy (PT) at a University of North Carolina (UNC) Healthcare System clinic

Exclusion Criteria:

* significant cognitive impairment
* neurological disorders affecting gait
* systemic rheumatic disease
* hospitalization for a cardiovascular condition the past six months
* psychosis
* substance abuse disorder
* lower extremity surgery in the past year
* any other health conditions determined to be contraindications to a home exercise program
